metadata.claim_supported: `bin/lib.d.ts` has the ArrayBuffer/typed-array section but no `DataView` declaration in the corresponding buffer block; the comment at line 1195 mentions DataView, then the file proceeds to `ArrayBuffer`, `ArrayBufferView`, and typed arrays instead.
metadata.coverage_area: default library declarations around binary buffers
metadata.why_relevant: This is the shipped default lib file implicated by the issue; the relevant section shows the gap where `DataView` should appear.

metadata.claim_supported: `src/lib/es6.d.ts` includes the full `DataView` API: `interface DataView`, `DataViewConstructor`, and `declare var DataView`.
metadata.why_relevant: This provides the source-side definition that is missing from the checked-in `bin/lib.d.ts` snapshot.

metadata.claim_supported: `src/lib/es6.d.ts` also defines several other ES6 interfaces and constructors such as `Map`, `Set`, and `Promise`.
metadata.why_relevant: The issue title says `DataView and other interfaces`; these declarations show the adjacent ES6 interfaces that belong in the same library set.

metadata.claim_supported: The compiler/service layer chooses the default lib file via `lib.d.ts` for non-ES6 targets, and `lib.es6.d.ts` only when the target is ES6.
metadata.why_relevant: This explains why an omission in `lib.d.ts` affects the baseline TypeScript experience.

metadata.claim_supported: The services layer also hardcodes `lib.d.ts` as the default library file name.
